8021.explanation:
The statement:

"Let peoples serve you, and nations bow down to you..."

…was made by Isaac when he was blessing his son Jacob, believing he was blessing Esau (Genesis 27:29). This blessing was part of the patriarchal blessing meant for the firstborn. Rebekah helped Jacob deceive Isaac into receiving this blessing.

Reference (RSV – Genesis 27:29):

“Let peoples serve you,
and nations bow down to you.
Be lord over your brothers,
and may your mother’s sons bow down to you!”

8039.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
8039.question_text: ''....To your tents, O Israel'' This was a signal for a
8039.explanation: The phrase "To your tents, O Israel" is used in the Bible in the context of a rebellion or a call to separation. It is notably found in the Old Testament in the account of the rebellion against King Rehoboam, the son of Solomon. After Rehoboam's harsh response to the request for lighter burdens from the northern tribes, the phrase is used by the people of Israel to announce the start of a rebellion against the House of David. (1 Kings 12:16).

8070.question_text: The miracle which Jesus performed on the sabbath was the healing of the
8070.explanation:
The miracle which Jesus performed on the Sabbath by healing a man was the healing of the man with the withered hand

This account is found in Matthew 12:9-14, Mark 3:1-6, and Luke 6:6-11.

Matthew 12:9-14 (RSV): 

9 And he went on from there, and entered their synagogue. 10 And behold, there was a man with a withered hand. And they asked him, “Is it lawful to heal on the sabbath?” so that they might accuse him. 11 He said to them, “What man of you, if he has one sheep and it falls into a pit on the sabbath, will not lay hold of it and lift it out? 12 Of how much more value is a man than a sheep! So it is lawful to do good on the sabbath.” 13 Then he said to the man, “Stretch out your hand.” And the man stretched it out, and it was restored, whole like the other. 14 But the Pharisees went out and took counsel against him, how to destroy him.

40475.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
40475.question_text: On the island of Malta, Paul healed a man who was
40475.explanation:
In Acts 28:8, while Paul and his companions were shipwrecked on the island of Malta, Paul healed Publius' father, who was sick with dysentery:

"It happened that the father of Publius lay sick with fever and dysentery. And Paul visited him and prayed, and putting his hands on him, healed him."

This event occurs after Paul was bitten by a viper and survived, which caused the Maltese people to believe he was a god. When Paul healed Publius' father, it further confirmed his divine power and God's presence with him.
